items.title: Finding the Volume Generated When a Shape is Rotated About the X-Axis

sections.normalized_html: The figure shown above is rotated [MATH: 360^\circ] about the [MATH: x]-axis. What is the volume of the corresponding solid of revolution?
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/39a2c51050dc7233646f046b262a9249]

The figure shown above is rotated [MATH: 360^\circ] about the [MATH: x]-axis. What is the volume of the corresponding solid of revolution?

sections.normalized_html:
Our solid of revolution is a hemisphere with radius [MATH: r=2.]

We can find the volume of a hemisphere using the formula

[MATH: V|= (1)/(2) ⋅ (4)/(3)πr^{3}; = (2)/(3)πr^{3}.]

Substituting [MATH: r=2] into the formula, we obtain

[MATH: V = \dfrac{2}{3}\pi (2)^3 = \dfrac{16}{3} \pi.]

items.title: Finding the Volume Generated When a Shape is Rotated About the Y-Axis

sections.normalized_html: The figure shown above is rotated [MATH: 360^\circ] about the [MATH: y]-axis. What is the volume of the corresponding solid of revolution?
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/30753dae8005ae13f164d05068979773]

The figure shown above is rotated [MATH: 360^\circ] about the [MATH: y]-axis. What is the volume of the corresponding solid of revolution?

sections.normalized_html:
Our solid of revolution is a conical frustum. The radii of the bases are [MATH: r=1] and [MATH: R=3,] and the height of the frustum is [MATH: h=5-2=3.]

We can find the volume of a conical frustum using the formula

[MATH: V = \dfrac{\pi}{3} h (R^2 + r^2 + R r).]

Substituting

[MATH: r = 1, \qquad R = 3, \qquad h = 3]

into the formula, we obtain

[MATH: V|= (π)/(3)(3)(3^{2} + 1^{2} + 3 ⋅ 1); = (π)/(3)(3)(13); = 13π.]
